comments.author: @regulus9181
comments.text: The video is a good attempt but it’s still riddled with obvious mistakes. Burundi maintains more battalions and militiamen inside the Congo than Rwanda ever does. Yet you assume the opposite. You say Rwanda receives more foreign aid than others, but also admit that aid to Rwanda has ended. You complain that the president in Rwanda obtained too many votes and hold it against the country. Remarkably you don’t mention that in the latest election JUST LAST YEAR, the ruling party in Burundi claimed not 99.99%, but a complete 100% of the seats so that Burundi is the one with a single-party parliament.

comments.author: @TheEarthEngineOfficial
comments.text: The Congo–Nile divide detail really stood out — two neighbours sharing the same plateau and the same colonial starting point, yet one ends up with the lake and the old capital while the other bets everything on gorilla permits and clean governance. It makes me wonder how much of the gap is geography and how much is the choices made after 1994. The $300-per-person crossover point was the most striking number in the whole video.
